items.title: AMD, Arm, and Qualcomm invest $60M in self-driving startup Wayve

featured_image.name: Can Wayve make London a self-driving city?

items.description:
Three of the world's largest chipmakers have joined forces to back Wayve, the London-based autonomous driving startup, investing a combined $60 million as part of an extension to its Series D funding round. AMD, Arm, and Qualcomm Ventures announced the investment on Wednesday, deepening the semiconductor industry's bet on a software-first approach to self-driving cars.[1][2]

The deal means Wayve now counts all four major automotive chip suppliers — including Nvidia, which invested in the original round — among its shareholders, giving the startup relationships across essentially every compute platform an automaker might use.[2]

items.title: MIT quantum sensor measures multiple properties at once

featured_image.name: Diamond-based quantum sensor technology for fast magnetic ...

items.description: Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology have developed a quantum sensor capable of measuring several physical properties simultaneously, overcoming a long-standing limitation of solid-state sensors that has confined them to reading only one quantity at a time.

items.title: Inflation climbs in India, Greece, and France as energy costs surge

featured_image.name: Here's the inflation breakdown for March 2026 — in one chart - CNBC

items.description: Fresh data released this week showed inflation accelerated in India, Greece, and France during March, with rising energy and food prices fanning price pressures across three continents amid the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East.

items.title: Iran threatens to block Red Sea trade as US blockade chokes its ports

featured_image.name: US military says blockade of Iran ports ‘completely’ halts economic trade

items.description:
Iran's armed forces warned on Wednesday that they would disrupt trade across the Red Sea, the Persian Gulf, and the Sea of Oman if the United States continues its naval blockade of Iranian ports, dramatically raising the stakes in one of the world's most critical shipping corridors as a fragile ceasefire hangs in the balance.

Ali Abdollahi, commander of Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters — the country's highest operational command — delivered the threat on Iranian state television. "The powerful armed forces of the Islamic Republic will not allow any exports or imports to continue in the Persian Gulf, the Sea of Oman, and the Red Sea," Abdollahi said, according to AFP. He argued that the US blockade "creates insecurity for Iran's commercial vessels and oil tankers" and constitutes "a prelude" to violating the two-week ceasefire brokered by Pakistan on April 8.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Chinese tanker defies US blockade as Trump preps for Xi summit

featured_image.name: China defies US blockade: Tanker sails through Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
The U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports is threatening to upend a carefully planned summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, scheduled for May 14 and 15 in Beijing, as Washington tightens its grip on a waterway that carries much of China's energy supply.

Trump met with U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue on Tuesday to prepare for the high-stakes visit, even as his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly escalated rhetoric against Beijing. Bessent accused China of being "an unreliable global partner" for hoarding oil during the Middle East war and warned that Chinese tankers carrying Iranian oil would be blocked. "They're not going to be able to get their oil. They can get oil. Not Iranian oil," Bessent told reporters in Washington.[1][2][3]

items.title: Northwestern chemists turn methane into methanol with 'bottled lightning'

featured_image.name: Scientists Are Using Lightning in a Bottle to Turn Methane Into ...

items.description: Northwestern University chemists have developed a plasma-based method to convert methane directly into methanol in a single step, bypassing the energy-intensive, multi-step industrial process used for decades. The study, published Wednesday in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, describes a technique that uses bursts of high-voltage electricity to generate miniature "lightning bolts" inside a glass reactor submerged in water.[1][2]

items.title: AI-designed proteins work as smart biosensors, study shows

featured_image.name: AI designs protein with applications for heart disease

items.description: Two studies published in Nature Biotechnology are pushing the boundaries of AI-driven protein engineering — one by turning AI-designed proteins into functional biosensors, and another by solving a persistent data bottleneck that has limited the technology's potential.

items.title: IAEA chief warns North Korea rapidly expanding nuclear weapons capacity

featured_image.name: IAEA chief raises 'serious concern' over N. Korea uranium enrichment

items.description: North Korea has made a "very serious increase" in its nuclear weapons production capabilities, the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency said Wednesday during a visit to Seoul, confirming a rapid expansion of activity across the country's key nuclear complex and the likely addition of a new uranium enrichment facility.

items.title: Satellite study finds urban methane emissions far exceed official estimates

featured_image.name: This potent greenhouse gas has been 'widely' underestimated, study ...

items.description: Methane emissions from cities around the world have climbed roughly 6 percent since 2019, far outpacing official government estimates, according to a study published this week in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The findings, based on satellite observations of 92 major urban centers, suggest that cities collectively account for about 10 percent of all human-caused methane emissions — nearly four times the output of the oil and gas "ultra-emitters" that have drawn the bulk of regulatory attention.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Sperm whale clicks contain vowel-like sounds, new study finds

featured_image.name: We're one step closer to understanding the sperm whale 'alphabet'

items.description: Sperm whales produce click patterns that contain vowel-like sounds strikingly similar to those found in human speech, according to new research published in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B. The study, led by UC Berkeley linguist Gašper Beguš and collaborators from Project CETI (Cetacean Translation Initiative), deepens what scientists know about one of the most complex communication systems in the animal kingdom.[1][2]

items.title: Google rolls out Gemini Personal Intelligence globally, excluding Europe

featured_image.name: Google is expanding Personal Intelligence to Gemini users ...

items.description: Google on Monday began rolling out its Personal Intelligence feature for Gemini to users globally, extending the AI personalization tool beyond the United States for the first time since its debut in January. The expansion, which covers paid subscribers on AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra plans, notably excludes the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.[1][2]

items.title: Pope Leo celebrates Mass at St. Augustine's basilica in Algeria

featured_image.name: ALGERIA-VATICAN-DIPLOMACY

items.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass on Tuesday at the Basilica of St. Augustine in Annaba, Algeria, completing a deeply personal pilgrimage to the land where one of Christianity's most influential thinkers lived and died — and marking the first time a pope has ever set foot in the North African country.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran restores limited internet for businesses after 46-day blackout

featured_image.name: Iran Internet Blackout Eases Slightly as Businesses Face ...

items.description:
Iran has begun restoring a sliver of internet connectivity to select businesses after a nationwide blackout that has now stretched past six weeks, in what observers describe as an attempt to stem mounting economic damage rather than a meaningful loosening of digital controls.

State-backed telecom firms are offering a "pro internet" package that companies can apply for through a formal identity verification process, according to digital rights group ASL19. Applicants must explain why they need connectivity and provide supporting documentation to receive access to online services outside Iran, ASL19 and fellow monitoring group Miaan Group said.[1][2]

items.title: About 250 missing after Rohingya boat capsizes in Andaman Sea

featured_image.name: Hundreds missing after Rohingya boat capsizes in Andaman Sea: UN

items.description:
Around 250 people, including Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals, are feared missing after a Malaysia-bound trawler capsized in the Andaman Sea, the United Nations said on Tuesday in a joint statement by the UNHCR and the International Organization for Migration.[1][2][3]

The vessel departed from Teknaf in southern Bangladesh around April 4 carrying an estimated 250 to 280 men, women, and children before sinking on approximately April 9 "due to heavy winds, rough seas, and overcrowding," according to the UNHCR. Only nine survivors have been found, raising fears that the rest perished at sea.[2][4][5]

items.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to direct negotiations after first talks in over 30 years

featured_image.name: Israel, Lebanon Agree to Launch Direct Talks After 'Productive' Washington Meeting

items.description: Israel and Lebanon on Tuesday agreed to begin direct peace negotiations following what the U.S. State Department called "productive discussions" at the first high-level meeting between the two governments in more than three decades. The agreement, reached after talks hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State Department in Washington, sets the stage for formal negotiations at "a mutually agreed time and venue," according to a department statement.[1][2]

items.title: OECD warns fuel-tax relief risks repeating 2022 mistakes amid oil crisis

featured_image.name: Crude Oil Prices Jump on Fears of a Wider Conflict in the Middle East

items.description: The ongoing war in the Middle East, which has disrupted roughly a fifth of global oil supply since Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in early March, is fueling a fierce debate over the world's dependence on fossil fuels — even as governments rush to cushion consumers from soaring energy costs.

items.title: Trump says US-Iran talks could resume in Pakistan within 48 hours

featured_image.name: Trump says he believes US is close to reaching a new Iran ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump signaled on Tuesday that diplomatic negotiations with Iran could resume in Pakistan within the next 48 hours, reversing his dismissive tone from just days earlier when he said he did not care whether Tehran returned to the table.

In an interview with the New York Post, Trump told reporters stationed in Islamabad, "You should really remain there, as something might unfold in the next 48 hours, and our interest in visiting is increasing." He praised Pakistan's Army Chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, calling his handling of the negotiations "exceptional" and citing it as a key reason for returning to the Pakistani capital.[1][2][3]

items.title: Europe plans Hormuz shipping mission excluding U.S.

featured_image.name: France to deploy almost a dozen warships and mull Hormuz ...

items.description:
European powers led by France and the United Kingdom are assembling a post-war coalition to secure shipping through the Strait of Hormuz that would deliberately exclude the United States, Israel, and Iran as "belligerent" parties, according to The Wall Street Journal. French President Emmanuel Macron outlined the plan on Tuesday, calling for an international defensive operation built around nations not involved in the fighting, as the transatlantic rift over the war widens into a concrete institutional split.[1]

The initiative, announced by both Macron and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer on X, envisions a conference "in the coming days" bringing together countries willing to contribute to what Macron described as "a peaceful multinational mission aimed at restoring freedom of navigation in the strait". "This strictly defensive mission, separate from the warring parties to the conflict, is intended to be deployed as soon as circumstances permit," Macron said. European diplomats have indicated that European vessels would not operate under American command.[2][3][4][1]

items.title: Scientists find 6,000 km³ of hidden magma beneath Tuscany

featured_image.name: Super magma reservoirs discovered beneath Tuscany

items.description: Two studies published this month are reshaping scientists' understanding of what lies beneath some of the world's most geologically active regions, with one finding that Yellowstone's magma originates far shallower than long believed and another uncovering a vast hidden magma reservoir beneath the rolling hills of Tuscany.

items.title: New footage shows Artemis II capsule opening after Moon mission splashdown

featured_image.name: NASA's Artemis II crew helped by Navy exiting the capsule in new closeup video

items.description: Four days after splashing down in the Pacific Ocean, newly released footage is offering a closer look at the recovery of NASA's Artemis II crew following their 10-day journey around the Moon — the first crewed lunar mission in more than half a century.
